narratives.Description: gate(agents-md): invert agents-entry propagation contract from full-text-mirror to pointer-sufficient
narratives.Overview:
Parent epic: #2369 · Predecessor context: #1882

## What

Invert the propagation contract `agents_entry_contract.test.ts` (#2111) from "rule text MUST be present in both files" to "a pointer is sufficient; the rule body lives in a skill/pack."

## Why

This contract currently forces full-text mirroring of ~10 rule blocks (value-feedback, eval, deterministic-questions, review-surface, session-ritual, WIP, etc.) into the always-on surface. #1882 trimmed *rationale* but left the *rules* full-text and mirrored — which is precisely why the diet plateaued. No relocation of rule bulk (parent epic #2369, Wave 2) is possible while the contract mandates the bulk stay in the always-on file.

## Scope

- Change the marker-list semantics: enforce that a **pointer** to each relocated rule's canonical home is present, rather than the rule's full text.
- Preserve the deterministic guarantee — a relocated rule must still be reachable and its pointer verified.
- **Three distinct relocation targets (per parent DD-1/DD-2), each a different pointer shape the contract must recognize:**
  - **pointer-to-skill** — workflow procedures relocated to a skill; the pointer resolves to a SKILL.md whose frontmatter carries the routing metadata.
  - **pointer-to-gate** — cross-cutting guardrails whose enforcement is a deterministic `task verify:*` gate; the always-on surface keeps only a terse one-line imperative + the gate reference.
  - **pointer-to-doc** — reference/rationale and *contextual* guardrails relocated to the lazy doc tree (main.md/docs/packs), reachable behind a runtime-detect pointer (precedent #2157).
- The contract must verify the *right* pointer shape per relocated item, and must NOT require the rule body itself in the always-on file for any of the three.

## Acceptance

- Contract enforces pointer-presence (skill / gate / doc), not full-text mirroring, and validates the pointer shape per relocated item.
- Universal guardrails may retain a one-line always-on imperative (DD-2); the contract permits this without demanding the full rule body.
- `task check` green.

Wave 1 — prerequisite for all relocation slices.
